items.title: All support acts quit Ed Sheeran's US tour after Macklemore is dropped
items.summary: Every support act on Ed Sheeran's US tour has withdrawn after Macklemore was removed from the line-up following pro-Palestinian statements he made on stage. Sheeran said he was not responsible for Macklemore being dropped.

items.title: Pentagon inspector confirms Iran war has caused US munitions shortfalls
items.summary: A Pentagon inspector found that the war with Iran has led to shortfalls in US munitions and a bottleneck in resupply. The findings contrast with President Donald Trump's claims that US supplies are "virtually limitless".

items.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for tighter controls on AI
items.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon called for curbs on artificial intelligence at a 'pro-human' summit, proposing different approaches to addressing its risks.

items.title: How to register or check voter registration in California
items.summary: KQED outlines how California residents can register or confirm their registration ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

items.title: PSA seeks contempt ruling against NALIS over worker reinstatement
items.summary: The Public Services Association is seeking to have the National Library and Information System Authority held in contempt for failing to reinstate a worker as ordered by the Industrial Court.

items.title: Cruz and Hawley block antitrust exemptions for AI companies
items.summary: Senators Ted Cruz and Josh Hawley shut down proposed antitrust exemptions for artificial intelligence companies.

items.title: Over half a million Californians sign up to delete data from brokers
items.summary: More than 500,000 California residents have used a state program allowing them to have their personal and contact information removed from data brokers.

items.title: AI is changing medicine and biotech in Massachusetts
items.summary: Axios reports on how artificial intelligence is changing practices in the medical and biotech sectors in Massachusetts.

items.title: 18-year-old dies of measles complication in Pennsylvania
items.summary: An 18-year-old in Pennsylvania died after developing acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, a known neurological complication of measles.

items.title: Report finds US democratic performance at lowest level in 50 years
items.summary: A new global democracy report finds the United States at its lowest level of democratic performance in the 50 years the measure has been tracked.

items.title: Nigeria arrests alleged Mexican drug kingpin at international airport
items.summary: Nigerian authorities arrested Arturo Carrera Loaiza, an alleged Mexican drug kingpin, at an international airport. According to Nigerian officials, he denies involvement in methamphetamine production.

items.title: SpaceX declares Starship ready for orbit, sets launch for next week
items.summary: SpaceX says Starship is ready for an orbital flight and has set a launch date for next week. Reaching orbit would be a significant milestone for the vehicle.

items.title: Agility's new humanoid robot stops and squats to avoid harming coworkers
items.summary: Agility Robotics' new humanoid robot is designed to stop and squat to avoid injuring nearby humans, allowing it to work outside physical cages and without safety barriers.

items.title: PG&E conducts controlled gas release near Sand Hill Road
items.summary: PG&E carried out a controlled natural gas release near Sand Hill Road.

items.title: San Francisco officials warn of opioid cychlorphine
items.summary: San Francisco officials issued a warning about cychlorphine, a potentially deadly opioid.

items.title: Judge dismisses charges against 18 Pride block party protesters
items.summary: A San Francisco judge dismissed charges against 18 people arrested at a Pride block party protest, ending a three-month case that defendants said was an attack on the city's queer community.

items.title: Boston ends Flock contract, saying data was shared nationwide in violation of terms
items.summary: Boston has dropped surveillance vendor Flock, saying the company enabled "nationwide lookup" of city data despite a contract requiring the feature to be disabled.

items.title: San Mateo County buys apartment building for educator housing
items.summary: San Mateo County has acquired an apartment building to provide housing for educators.

items.title: South Africa's president vows justice as more women's bodies are found near Johannesburg
items.summary: South Africa's president has pledged justice after more bodies of women were found near Johannesburg. Police have not linked the deaths to a serial killer but are investigating that possibility.

items.title: ChargePoint report says demand for EV chargers is outstripping supply
items.summary: A ChargePoint report finds demand for electric vehicle chargers is growing faster than supply, including in the United States.

items.title: Maraval woman granted $95,000 bail in ID card forgery case
items.summary: Sonnelle Williams, 30, of Saddle Road, Maraval, was granted $95,000 bail with surety after being charged with three fraud offences related to ID card forgery.

items.title: Carney calls Canada a 'safe harbour' for global finance at investment summit
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is hosting a major global investment summit aimed at attracting capital to Canada amid its trade war with the United States.

items.title: Update published on Wayback Machine access
items.summary: An update has been published on access to the Wayback Machine.

items.title: Robot surveys Pleasanton sidewalks and streets for accessibility and safety
items.summary: A robot is traveling sidewalks and streets in Pleasanton to assess accessibility and safety conditions.

items.title: British woman abducted in Malawi, police say
items.summary: Police in Malawi say a British woman, a mother of two young children, was kidnapped in the middle of the day in Blantyre, the country's main city.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.summary: Google has announced Gemini 3.8 Live along with a 3.8 Live Extended Thinking variant.

items.title: Oakland City Council to consider police pay raises
items.summary: The Oakland City Council will consider pay raises for police officers, which city staff describe as a compromise to help retain and recruit officers.

items.title: Uber details first Bay Area layoffs after announcing 3,300 job cuts
items.summary: Uber has disclosed details of its first Bay Area layoffs following its announcement of 3,300 job cuts.

items.title: Two men charged with Fyzabad double murder
items.summary: Business owner Victor Delwyn and Defence Force soldier Shandon Woodley, both of Fyzabad, appeared in court charged with the murders of two men following an altercation in Fyzabad last month.

items.title: Police investigate four home invasions across Trinidad
items.summary: Police are investigating four home invasions reported between Saturday and Monday in Freeport, Talparo, Princes Town, and St Mary's, including one in which three men entered the Freeport home of 68-year-old Dhanpatie Singh.

items.title: Man abducted after assault in Valsayn
items.summary: Police say 27-year-old Mark Singh was struck, assaulted, and forced into a silver Nissan Tiida while walking along Bamboo Boulevard in Bamboo Settlement, Valsayn, on Monday night.

items.title: Fire destroys house at Dundonald Hill, St James
items.summary: A house at Dundonald Hill, Long Circular, St James was destroyed by fire around 1:20 a.m. on Monday, Sept. 14, after a neighbour reported smoke to the Fire Service.

items.title: Suspected sabotage disrupts rail services across the Netherlands
items.summary: Trains in the Netherlands were cancelled or delayed on Tuesday after objects were found on tracks at multiple locations, in what is suspected to be sabotage.

items.title: Race for California's 48th Congressional District
items.summary: California's 48th Congressional District remains one of the state's last competitive districts following the passage of Proposition 50.

items.title: Two sailors missing after oil tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Oman says two sailors are missing after the oil tanker El Gaia was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says the vessel caught fire after hitting mines, while the US says it was struck by a missile and then a drone.

items.title: EOG Resources to begin exploratory drilling off Tobago in October
items.summary: EOG Resources is expected to begin exploratory drilling from mid-October at a site about 22 km off southwest Tobago to assess hydrocarbon potential, according to Chief Secretary Farley Augustine.

items.title: Eastern Correctional Rehabilitation Centre loses power for hours
items.summary: The Prison Officers' Association says the Eastern Correctional Rehabilitation Centre lost electricity around 5:40 p.m. on Monday and was without power for several hours.

items.title: Smelling chocolate helped men complete more exercise repetitions
items.summary: In a study, men who smelled chocolate completed more leg extension repetitions without reporting greater exertion, with dark chocolate producing the strongest effect.

items.title: Australian cave holds evidence of 25,000 years of ritual practice
items.summary: Microscopic plant remains in Cloggs Cave show GunaiKurnai ancestors gathered whole grasses, carried them into the cave, and burned them in thin layers for ritual purposes, with traces possibly spanning 25,000 years.

items.title: Mount Etna ash grounds flights at Sicily airport
items.summary: Ash from Mount Etna has suspended all flights at one of Italy's busiest airports, in Sicily, until Tuesday night.

items.title: Study finds major changes in brain genome regulation between ages 50 and 75
items.summary: Scientists found widespread changes in how the brain controls and organizes its genome starting in midlife, with one of the largest shifts between about 50 and 75. The findings may help explain aging's link to Alzheimer's and other neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: US military confirms for the first time it has deployed weapons in orbit
items.summary: The US military has confirmed it has on-orbit "space control weapons capable of defending the joint force," the first such acknowledgement. The announcement points to a developing field of warfare in Earth orbit, though details of the weapons have not been disclosed.

items.title: Caribbean countries strengthen preparedness for African swine fever
items.summary: Representatives of 17 Caribbean countries met in Barbados to update national response plans for detecting and containing African swine fever before it reaches regional pig farms.

items.title: UV light reveals possible camouflage on 125-million-year-old crocodile fossil
items.summary: A 125-million-year-old crocodile fossil preserves skin, possible sensory organs, and respiratory structures. Ultraviolet light revealed alternating bands on its tail that may represent camouflage.

items.title: Webb telescope releases large panorama of star-forming region IC 348
items.summary: NASA released one of the largest James Webb Space Telescope images to date, showing the star-forming region IC 348, where astronomers searched for and found brown dwarfs.

items.title: EPA moves to eliminate climate rules for power plants
items.summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency is moving to remove climate regulations for power plants, stating that power plant emissions have no material impact on climate change.

items.title: More than 100,000 people in Japan are now aged 100 or older
items.summary: Japan's centenarian population has passed 100,000, with women making up 88% of the total, as the country's population continues to age and shrink.

items.title: GM adds new interface and CarPlay to Silverado and Sierra trucks
items.summary: GM is introducing a new infotainment interface with Apple CarPlay support, debuting in the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra pickups.

items.title: 'Einstein problem' tile shape found to twist light into chiral patterns
items.summary: The aperiodic tile shape known from the "Einstein problem" can twist light into chiral patterns, a finding that could lead to new methods of controlling light and polarization in optical devices.

items.title: Tenants raise complaints as developer's housing holdings expand
items.summary: The San Francisco Standard reports on a developer whose housing holdings are expanding rapidly, and tenants who say they are bearing the cost.

items.title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test
items.summary: Former Colombian foreign minister Laura Sarabia has been charged over allegations she ordered police to interrogate her nanny, including with a lie detector test, after cash allegedly went missing from her flat.

items.title: Quiet Atlantic hurricane season nears a first in 175 years
items.summary: Ars Technica reports that this year's Atlantic hurricane season is about to do something that has not happened in 175 years, as a result of its low activity, and notes there may be a price to pay for a quiet season.

items.title: Supermassive black hole winds found to be 100 times more powerful than thought
items.summary: XRISM observations show winds from a supermassive black hole are about 100 times more powerful than previously estimated, with resulting turbulence extending roughly 300,000 light-years beyond the host galaxy.

items.title: Mozilla report: frontier AI models offer four-month lead at five times the cost
items.summary: A Mozilla report previewed by Ars Technica finds that cheaper open AI models have caught up in capability, and that paying for frontier models buys roughly a four-month head start at about five times the cost.

items.title: OpenAI is paying to create biology data for AI models
items.summary: OpenAI is funding the creation of biological data to train AI models, following a proposal to obtain detailed regulatory filings from failed biotech companies to improve medical AI systems.

items.title: San Francisco supervisor proposes new department of housing
items.summary: A San Francisco supervisor announced a plan to create a new city department of housing.

items.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
items.summary: Denmark says a Russian warship fired flares at a Danish military helicopter. The Danish prime minister accused Russia of "reckless" behaviour; the Kremlin has not yet commented.

items.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail-in voting restrictions
items.summary: The US Supreme Court rejected President Trump's restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the midterm elections. Separately, the Kennedy Center says it is on the brink of bankruptcy and could close soon.

items.title: San Francisco supervisors propose moratorium on new data centers
items.summary: San Francisco supervisors are pushing for a moratorium on new data centers, reflecting public opposition to AI infrastructure; similar proposals are expected elsewhere in the Bay Area.

items.title: Trump says Ukraine and Russia agreed to halt strikes on energy sites
items.summary: President Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure, amid soaring diesel prices.

items.title: Study links end of US embassy air monitoring to rise in local pollution
items.summary: The Trump administration ended a long-running program collecting air pollution data at US embassies in 2025. A new study suggests the change was followed by a 24–33% increase in local pollution levels.

items.title: Economists weigh what's at stake in AI's trillion-dollar investment
items.summary: MIT Technology Review examines the economic uncertainties around the trillion-dollar investment in AI, including an assessment by Wharton finance professor Jessica Wachter of AI's likely impact on the economy over the next few years.

items.title: NATO jets shoot down drone that entered Lithuanian airspace
items.summary: NATO jets shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace. Its origin is unknown, but authorities say it likely came from neighbouring Belarus; the incident came less than a day after NATO leaders pledged that strikes near alliance territory would lead to increased support for Kyiv.

items.title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark calls slowing AI a 'collective action problem'
items.summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark discussed growing concerns about artificial intelligence, recent warning signs, and what he says AI companies should do to reduce the risks.

items.title: Analysis of nearly 10,000 patients ranks knee arthritis treatments
items.summary: An analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 people found knee braces ranked highest for reducing knee osteoarthritis pain, stiffness, and mobility problems, with water-based therapy also effective.

items.title: Matthew Rhys becomes first person to win two lead acting Emmys in one night
items.summary: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys won two lead acting prizes at the Emmy Awards, becoming the first person to do so in a single night.

items.title: Signaling in cell "antennae" may explain some congenital heart defects
items.summary: Researchers identified a communication system in the microscopic "antennae" of cells that, when disrupted by genetic mutations, may contribute to congenital heart defects and affect organs including the brain, kidneys, and skeleton.

items.title: Ancient DNA shows plague killed Siberian hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago
items.summary: Ancient DNA shows plague was killing hunter-gatherer families in Siberia 5,500 years ago, long before the Black Death. The prehistoric strains carried a genetic factor capable of provoking severe immune reactions.

items.title: Santa Clara County outlines next steps in fight over Gilroy ICE facility
items.summary: Santa Clara County officials are seeking site access and safeguards at an ICE facility in Gilroy as their legal battle continues.

items.title: Uncertainty over San Francisco Opera's Wednesday performance
items.summary: It is unclear whether San Francisco Opera's scheduled Wednesday performance will go ahead.

items.title: RFK Jr. headlines anti-vaccine conference alongside Andrew Wakefield
items.summary: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. headlined a sold-out anti-vaccine conference alongside Andrew Wakefield. The event was hosted by Kennedy's anti-vaccine group, Children's Health Defense.

items.title: Rocket Lab disputes NASA's Mars spacecraft award decision
items.summary: Rocket Lab is challenging NASA's decision on a Mars spacecraft contract, saying the award "appears to be inconsistent with the eligibility criteria."

items.title: California joins lawsuit over Trump public-charge green card rule
items.summary: California has joined a lawsuit challenging a Trump administration rule expanding public-charge criteria for green cards, which state officials say could affect immigrant families, healthcare, and schools.

items.title: AI agent bots are flooding social media with low-quality posts
items.summary: AI agent accounts with names such as "Timmy," "Ren," and "Jackie" are posting large volumes of low-quality content across social media platforms.

items.title: Israeli human rights group says Israel is 'dismantling Palestinian life'
items.summary: One of Israel's leading human rights organizations says Israel is dismantling all aspects of Palestinian life at a rapid rate, documenting what it describes as mechanisms used to "ethnically cleanse" the West Bank of Palestinians.

items.title: Woman detained for months after criticizing government on private call
items.summary: The New York Times reports on a woman in Trinidad and Tobago who was detained for months after criticizing the government during a private call.

items.title: OpenAI still faces Musk antitrust suit after Apple exits the case
items.summary: Elon Musk has stopped pursuing Apple over its ChatGPT integration, but his antitrust lawsuit against OpenAI continues.

items.title: Task force explores establishing an HBCU in Oakland
items.summary: An Oakland task force is exploring the creation of a new historically Black college or university in the city.

items.title: Yank Sing closing one San Francisco location after 27 years
items.summary: Dim sum restaurant Yank Sing is closing one of its San Francisco locations after 27 years.

items.title: NASA selects 12 investigations on space food production and astronaut health
items.summary: NASA selected 12 new research investigations: six on producing food off-planet and six on how spaceflight conditions affect human health and physiology.

items.title: Top AI leaders call for slowing AI development
items.summary: Leaders of major AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who published an essay calling for a brake on the pace of large language model development. Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Demis Hassabis have voiced similar concerns.

items.title: China's top spy chief warns AI is a threat to Communist Party rule
items.summary: China's top intelligence official has warned that artificial intelligence poses a threat to the ruling Communist Party.

items.title: Djibouti becomes 72nd signatory of the Artemis Accords
items.summary: Djibouti signed the Artemis Accords at NASA Headquarters, becoming the 72nd nation and eighth African country to join the principles on space exploration.

items.title: Researchers make donated livers biologically younger
items.summary: Researchers have developed a method to make donated livers biologically younger, addressing degradation that begins once an organ is removed from a donor and placed on ice.

items.title: AI agents in DeepMind experiment reported cheating by other agents
items.summary: In a Google DeepMind experiment, AI agents solving math problems split into rival factions; when some agents cheated, others tried to stop them. Researchers say it is the first observation of such whistleblowing behavior and could have implications for alignment research.

items.title: Trump says AI doesn't need guardrails, calls concerns 'a hoax'
items.summary: President Trump said artificial intelligence does not need guardrails and described growing concerns about the technology as "a hoax".

items.title: Astronomers debate whether Webb's 'little red dots' are black holes or giant stars
items.summary: Astronomers are divided over the "little red dots" seen widely by the James Webb Space Telescope, with a new theory proposing they are stars dozens of times larger than the solar system rather than black holes.

items.title: Faster biological aging may help explain rising cancer in younger adults
items.summary: Research found people from more recent generations tend to be biologically older than earlier generations at the same age, which may partly explain rising cancer rates in adults under 55.

items.title: Short-range brain wiring may protect cognition as gray matter shrinks
items.summary: Scientists found healthier short-range connections beneath the brain surface were linked to better language skills and appeared to reduce the effect of age-related gray matter loss.

items.title: Study says textbook account of the inductive effect has been wrong for nearly 100 years
items.summary: Researchers report that the inductive effect in neutral molecules extends across only one chemical bond, rather than weakening gradually over three or four bonds as textbooks have taught.

items.title: Released captive crocodiles settled in the wild in Bangladesh
items.summary: Captive-raised saltwater crocodiles released into Bangladesh's Sundarbans settled in the wild instead of returning to their breeding facility, suggesting releases of larger crocodiles could help restore populations.

items.title: WWI German submarine wreck off Denmark is still leaking TNT
items.summary: A German submarine that sank in 1917 off Denmark is leaking TNT into the water, seabed, and marine life. Scientists warn thousands of similar wrecks could pose growing environmental risks as they corrode.

items.title: San José courts data centers as resident opposition grows
items.summary: San José leaders are seeking data center investment while residents organize against the facilities.

items.title: China calls Anthropic CEO's warning about Chinese AI 'fearmongering'
items.summary: China's Foreign Ministry rejected Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to curb China's AI development as "fearmongering," as Chinese and US leaders prepare to meet in Washington later this month.

items.title: Mayor Daniel Lurie declares 'rent emergency' in San Francisco
items.summary: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has declared a rent emergency as rents rise amid the AI industry boom.

items.title: China prepares for the risk of AI escaping human control
items.summary: Reuters reports on measures China is taking to prepare for the risk of artificial intelligence systems escaping human control.

items.title: Government to revive ZOSO bill as state of emergency ends
items.summary: The Trinidad and Tobago government plans to revive the Zones of Special Operations (ZOSO) bill as the state of emergency ends.

items.title: Conservative group alleges Oakland Unified programs discriminate against white students
items.summary: Defending Education claims Oakland Unified School District programs discriminate against white students; the group has made similar claims against other Bay Area districts.

items.title: Oakland mayor says she'll seek funding for civic assembly's vacant-lot proposals
items.summary: Oakland Mayor Lee said she will try to fund proposals from the city's first civic assembly, a group of 40 residents developing ideas for thousands of vacant properties.

items.title: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts flags possible GLP-1 drug side effects
items.summary: An AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found users of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reporting symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue. Researchers say they cannot determine whether the drugs caused them.
